items.name: HL · Readable receipt
items.what: The 2.2 solved problem: for each new Orders row, one Google Sheets · Update a Row fills phone_clean (+234 format), first_name, delivery_day (next day, never a Sunday) and a readable receipt_text, all with functions inside the fields. 2 credits per order however many functions it uses. It reproduces the lesson's "Hi Mrs!" title bug on purpose; fixing it is the Silver mission.
build: 1 · Google Sheets › Watch New Rows: business Google connection; Spreadsheet = Harvest Lane; Sheet = Orders; Table contains headers = Yes; Limit = 10; start From now on.
2 · Google Sheets › Update a Row: same spreadsheet; Sheet = Orders; Row number = 1. Row number (the trigger's row number); leave A–N empty so the original columns are untouched, and fill only:

phone_clean (column O) = {{if(substring(replace(1.phone; /[^0-9]/g; emptystring); 0; 1) = "0"; "+234" + substring(replace(1.phone; /[^0-9]/g; emptystring); 1; 20); "+" + replace(1.phone; /[^0-9]/g; emptystring))}}
delivery_day (column Q) = {{if(formatDate(addDays(1.created_at; 1); "d") = "0"; formatDate(addDays(1.created_at; 2); "dddd D MMM"); formatDate(addDays(1.created_at; 1); "dddd D MMM"))}}

receipt_text (column R) = Hi {{startcase(lower(get(split(trim(1.customer_name); " "); 1)))}}! Order {{1.order_id}} received. [new line] Total: ₦{{formatNumber(1.total; 0; "."; ",")}} [new line] Delivery: {{if(formatDate(addDays(1.created_at; 1); "d") = "0"; formatDate(addDays(1.created_at; 2); "dddd D MMM"); formatDate(addDays(1.created_at; 1); "dddd D MMM"))}}, {{ifempty(1.delivery_window; "time to be confirmed")}}. [new line] Thank you for choosing Harvest Lane.
Arguments are separated by semicolons; emptystring is Make's keyword for ""; substring counts from 0, get() from 1; MM is month, mm is minutes, d is the weekday number (0 = Sunday).
Optional title fix (Silver mission): inside first_name, wrap trim(1.customer_name) as replace(trim(1.customer_name); /^(mr|mrs|miss|dr|chief)\.?\s+/i; emptystring) before split().
setup: In Make, set your organisation and profile time zone to Africa/Lagos before running anything with dates (2.2).

Orders tab layout the blueprints assume (row 1 = headers): A order_id, B created_at, C customer_id, D customer_name, E delivery_date, F delivery_fee, G status, H items_total, I total (the 0.4 columns), then J phone, K channel, L delivery_window, M customer_email, N payment_link. If your columns differ, open each Google Sheets module after import and re-pick the columns; the build list names every field.
Add four new headers to Orders: O phone_clean, P first_name, Q delivery_day, R receipt_text. The automation fills them in.
In Make: Scenarios → Create a new scenario → the three-dot menu at the bottom → Import Blueprint → choose this file.
Connect Google Sheets in module 1 and module 2 with the business Google account, pick the spreadsheet and the Orders tab in both, and choose From now on in module 1.
In module 2, check Row number is mapped to the trigger's row number and that the four formulas sit in columns O–R. Re-drop any field that shows empty after import.
Schedule it like 2.1 (hourly, 07:00–21:00), or keep it switched off and use Run once while you practise.
items.test: Add a Saturday order (created_at on a Saturday) for "  mrs ADEBAYO ", phone 0803 123 4567, total 26500, delivery_window afternoon, and Run once. The row gets phone_clean +2348031234567, delivery_day Monday 12 Oct style (never Sunday) and the receipt "Hi Mrs! Order HL-0061 received. Total: ₦26,500. Delivery: Monday …, afternoon." Add a Friday order and one with a blank delivery_window (it says "time to be confirmed"). Each order costs 2 credits: the trigger and the one Update module.

walk.title: Build it: a receipt customers can actually read
walk.sample: Saturday order HL-0061 · "  mrs ADEBAYO " · 0803 123 4567 · total 26500 · afternoon

steps.say: Before anything with dates, set your Make time zone to Africa slash Lagos, or delivery days come out a day off.
show: Organisation and profile time zone: Africa/Lagos

steps.say: Same trigger as 2.1: Watch New Rows on the Orders tab, starting from now on.
We add just one more module, Update a Row, and point it at the trigger's own row number, so we write back to the same order.
We leave the original columns empty so nothing gets overwritten. Only the four new columns, O to R, get filled.
For the phone, strip everything that isn't a digit, then swap a leading zero for plus two three four. One format, so one customer never becomes three.
For the first name: trim, split on the space, take item one, then tidy the case. Remember, get counts from one in Make.
Delivery is the next day, unless that's a Sunday, when it moves to Monday. The little d token gives the weekday number, and zero means Sunday.
The receipt mixes plain text with formulas. The naira sign and commas are for people only; the total column keeps a plain number you can sum.
Watch the separators: Make uses semicolons between arguments, and emptystring for an empty value. Commas make the formula invalid.
show: if(a; b; c), not if(a, b, c)

steps.say: Run once with a Saturday order. Notice the receipt says Hi Mrs. That's the title bug, and realistic test names are how you catch it before customers do.
Count the credits: the trigger and one update, two credits per order, however many functions you used.

walk.end: Run it with a Saturday order, a Friday order and a blank delivery window, and check no receipt ever names a Sunday.
